lockup.summary: The company, its officers, directors and nearly all other shareholders agreed not to sell shares for 180 days after the prospectus date, unless the lead underwriters give written consent.

what: Aspen Neuroscience is developing a Parkinson's disease treatment made from a patient's own stem cells.
proceeds: It expects net proceeds of about $125.8 million. About $110.0 million is for a Phase 3 trial of its Parkinson's treatment, $8.0 million for its current trial and $4.0 million for microglia research. The rest is for general business needs.
risks: It is an early-stage company with a short history and no approved products, so its future is hard to judge.
It has lost a lot of money since it began, expects more losses, and may never turn a profit.
Its financial condition raises serious doubt about whether it can keep operating.
Even if this offering succeeds, it will need much more money, and failing to raise it could force cutbacks.
Raising more money could dilute shareholders, limit how it operates, or force it to give up rights to its technology.
